title: The Shepherd and the White Tablecloth
summary: On a green hill lives a poor shepherd with ten sheep and a little old knapsack. One day a lost little prince arrives, hungry and tired, and the shepherd has no bread, no cakes and no silk pillows... but at the bottom of the knapsack waits something white and clean. When a white tablecloth one day waves from the palace tower, a big surprise begins. Baa-baa! A rhyming story based on a parable of the Baal Shem Tov.
pages:
On a green hill, by a tree and a spring,
sat a poor shepherd with a little old knapsack — and hardly a thing.
No money, no crown, and his clothes were worn and cheap —
Baa-baa! Baa-baa! cry all the sheep!

Suddenly, from the bushes, out came a little lad,
with a tiny gold crown on the blue-and-white cap he had.
"I'm the king's son," he whispered, "and I've lost my way,
I'm hungry, and thirsty, and very, very tired today."

The shepherd took his hand, as gently as a big brother would,
and led him to his hut, by the tree and the spring where it stood.
"A prince in my hut!" he cried, and he jumped with joy and glee,
"But how shall I honor him? Wait... just wait and see!"

He searched in his knapsack: no bread, no cakes at all,
no silken pillows, no soft beds, big or small.
And the sheep helped him search, digging deep —
Baa-baa! Baa-baa! cry all the sheep!

And at the bottom of the knapsack — look! Something white:
a linen tablecloth, clean as a cloud and bright.
He spread it on the table slowly, as if for a holiday,
and on the floor, soft as cake, a white blanket lay.

On the cloth was no bread, only a cup of cold water to drink,
but the shepherd served it like a royal waiter, quick as a wink!
And that night the king's son fell asleep on the blanket white,
with one sheep lying beside him, like a fat pillow for the night.

In the morning — ta-ra-ra! — trumpets sounded from the mountain high,
the king's horsemen came and found the missing prince nearby.
The prince folded the tablecloth and whispered, secret and low:
"When you see it waving — come to me, as fast as you can go!"

A day went by, and another, and another plain weekday,
and the shepherd gazed at the palace, big and far away.
Then suddenly — a white tablecloth! On the tower, among new flags above the keep!
Baa-baa! Baa-baa! cry all the sheep!

The shepherd came to the palace, his sheep behind him — tok-tok, in a line,
and the prince seated him up high, on a golden chair by the lamp so fine.
"A shepherd?!" asked the ministers. "We gave gold, and silk, and a crown!"
"And I — a cake as tall as a tower!" "And I — an elephant!" "And I gave even more — the finest gift in town!"

The prince smiled and pointed to the tower, high over every minister in the hall:
"He gave me the whitest, cleanest thing — the finest gift of all."
And on silken chairs, by a shepherd and ministers in robes that sweep —
Baa-baa! Baa-baa! cry all the sheep!
